![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/7e0a0b1860f316f7954e85b9d7f6567d9e0c05bf316cb8af3901037abe6fd17e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡5,\,{e}^{y}\le x\le 5\}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x={e}^{y}\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 5,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡x\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/3c95dd90ad02ab708f5893e47e7d7d0c8a212c18aed1972fb1bba1362181c383.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x)[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x)\cdot y\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-x)\,{|}_{1}^{5} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡5-5)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(1\operatorname{ln}⁡1-1) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\operatorname{ln}⁡5-5).\end{aligned}
$$
